_readme: Encounter move narration (Saga), v1. Ordinary turn-log lines for encounters-v0.1 (file docs/design/encounters-v0.1.md, repo commit 4c9be75, which is v0.1.1 plus the v0.1.2 bite-spam tells, the 13-round cap, and the v0.1.3 §2.9 edge rulings). Follows narrator-voice-v1: second person, present tense, no digits or number words, no game words, no saber colour, no pronouns for other cats. Asides are a separate bank and are not used during fight rounds. These lines are upright narrator colour; asides, if any, would be italic after the close. Selection: each list is tried in order, first matching when wins, the last entry has no when and is the default. Tells (§2.4a): before the player's turn, pick the shown foe move, then honest or feint. Honest and feint lines are written in the same register so they cannot be told apart by wording. Quick resolve reuses these lines (fights play the average table, hunts play Steady moves, courtship plays quick_resolve then the accept or reject roll). There is no crit in the spec, so there are no crit lines.

_schema.when: First match wins; last entry is the default and has no when. Matches if every key present is true. foeKind, kind and prey may be a string or a list. group is true for a pack or clan; Flint's group flag selects those tells. actor is you or foe. trait/band/who uses genetics bands (low at or below the low cut, high at or above the high cut, else baseline); who is target for courtship, player only if a later hook needs it. partner is true when a hunting partner is present. perk is feint (a Swipe that cannot be countered) or gift (courtship gift prey). repeat is half then spent. lethal is true for rival attacks, leadership challenges and wild enemies. injury is minor, serious or crippling, for guardian prey-reaction hooks. phase and result are hunt tags. size is small, medium or large.
_schema.tokens: {foeName} is a display name for the fight, spar or showdown opponent (a cat's name, or a phrase such as the hyena or the wolves). {name} is the courtship target or a hunting partner. {zoneName} is reserved and unused in this bank.
_schema.tells: Per foe move, honest and feint arrays. Flint picks the shown move, then the array. Group tells use when.group true. Do not offer flee tells for a wolf pack or a hyena clan (they never flee). Only a lone hyena flees; those tells are under when.foeKind hyena. Humans get no next-move tells: they do not pick moves (§2.9).
_schema.standoff: Ordinary narration for a human standoff, not a tell. Play while the standoff holds. No honest or feint keys: these lines never promise a coming move.
_schema.fights: Per move, outcome keys: swipe/bite/pounce have hit, miss, blocked, countered, hit_open. Pounce miss already shows the attacker left Open. blocked is a hit that meets Defend. countered is the return blow; play it only with a blocked hit (encounters §2.9: a miss gets no counter). Against humans, Intimidate success ends the encounter as they back off and you walk away unhurt; Intimidate fail is a spear jab (minor injury) and the standoff continues; Flee fail is a heavy spear wound (serious) and you drop what you carry. hit_open is a hit that lands while the target is Open. Defend has ready. Intimidate has success (Shaken) and fail. Flee has success and fail. The feint perk is a swipe entry with when.perk feint; it has no countered key.
_schema.hunt: Per phase and move: creep, rush_in, run_it_down, sprint, throat_bite, drag_down have success and fail. freeze has held (prey stays; next Stalk is closer) and drift (hunt ends, no injury roll). cut_it_off has a partner entry using {name}, then a solo default (Trail Reading). hamstring is large only; the default is written for large prey because the move is only offered then. Fail lines never claim an injury. second_lunge is a retry beat after a failed phase.
_schema.prey_reactions: Optional second beat, keyed by species. when.injury hooks are for the existing large-prey injury roll (guardian flavour). Do not play them unless an injury was actually rolled.
_schema.courtship: Reactions per move. Liked and disliked bands follow encounters §4.3; the default is the mid band (no swing). gift_prey is always welcome; the perk entry is warmer. back_off ends the attempt with no sting. accept and reject are the final roll. repeat.half and repeat.spent are a shared pool for a repeated move. repeat.half and repeat.spent replace the trait reaction and stand alone as the only line for that beat. quick_resolve is the bridge when courtship ends at the current Interest.
_schema.ends: yield.you / yield.foe (spar, scuffle or confront, then a default). fight_end.win / lose with lethal true or false; lethal lines do not assume death, which is a later roll. timeout.win / lose when the round cap is hit and one side still has the better of it; no equal-bar line is written. timeout.win / lose when the round cap is hit and one side still has the better of it. timeout_even.win is you winning as the defender of ground or a kill; timeout_even.lose is the foe winning as the defender; timeout_even.break_off is a wild fight or a scuffle, where there is no defender and both sides break off with no winner. showdown.win / lose is the display duel that can replace a mate rival challenge, not the turn-based fight.

_gaps: Hits against a Shaken foe have no separate wording. Shaken is the Intimidate success beat.
Band and group fights stay on the current build (encounters §2.7). This bank has no per-move lines for them.
Showdown is a display roll, not the turn engine. Only end win and lose are written; there is no start beat.
second_lunge flavour is not specified. A short retry beat is included. The spec does not say which failed phases it may retry, except that it retries one failed phase.
Loyalty is in the trait set but has no courtship move, so there are no loyalty-banded courtship lines.
No {preyName} token is used; species flavour is selected by when.prey. {zoneName} is reserved and unused.
There is no crit outcome in the spec.
_questions: Flint: should a hit on a Shaken foe use the ordinary hit lines, or do you want a later pass of wording?
Flint: is the gift perk's warmer set the right hook, or should it use the default gift lines?
Flint: Quick resolve fights and hunts can replay the move lines; is the courtship quick_resolve bridge wanted before the accept roll?
Tundra: confirm that sociability-high early yields in non-lethal fights reuse the ordinary yield lines.
Ochre: these are ordinary narration (upright, narrator colour), not asides.
